title: MaterialColor
description: A canonical colour: LINEAR sRGB with straight alpha, each channel a finite float in [0, 1]. 'Linear sRGB' is meant precisely: sRGB primaries and white point, with the sRGB transfer function DECODED, so r, g and b are linear-light values. These are NOT encoded/'gamma' sRGB values of the kind written as #E6D2B5 or rgb(230 210 181) in CSS or in a colour picker; those are transfer-encoded, and calling them linear is the exact ambiguity this contract removes. The difference is large, not academic: 0.5 encoded is 0.2159 linear. Conversion from an encoded value happens in exactly one place, studio_spatial.colors.srgb_encoded_channel_to_linear, and dividing an 8-bit value by 255 is explicitly NOT that conversion. `a` is a plain unitless coverage scalar in [0, 1] and carries NO transfer function — decoding alpha would be a category error. Linear is canonical because it is what Blender's Principled BSDF base_color expects, so no colour-space conversion happens at the Blender boundary — the same reasoning that makes METERS and RADIANS canonical. A colour NAME ('warm beige') is never representable here: names are interpreted above the worker, against a deliberately tiny deterministic palette or by a real provider, and arrive as explicit validated numbers. The palette is a convenience, not a restriction: any schema-valid explicit colour is acceptable. JSON cannot encode NaN/Infinity, so the finite rule is additionally enforced by the validation layer.

a.description: Straight alpha, unitless; 1 is fully opaque. Not transfer-encoded.
